bios.youtube_description:
Start at the Planck length, where known physics runs out, and keep doubling. How many doublings until you reach a galaxy? Guess before it ends.

Lumiera is science, drawn in light: physics, space, biology and math as short cinematic films, glowing on deep space. Each film asks one clear question and gives you time to guess. Then it acts out the answer: copies line up, counters climb, and the scale finally makes sense.

What you'll find here:
- Scale journeys, from the Planck length to the observable universe
- Life up close, from viruses to blood cells
- Space and light, from the Sun to the Milky Way
- Math you can watch happen

A new film every week. Every number is checked, every comparison is real, and no title promises more than the film delivers. If we get a number wrong, we pin the correction.

Lumiera, from lumière: light.

first_post.instagram_caption:
The Doubling.

Begin at the Planck length: 1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ m, where known physics runs out. Double it. Then again.

Step 66: a proton.
Step 116: you. Remember that one.
Step 205: the edge of the observable universe.

How many doublings to reach a galaxy? Guess before it ends, then leave your number in the comments.

Send it to a friend so they can guess first ✦
first_post.instagram_alt_text: Vertical animated film on a deep black, space-like background. A tiny glowing dot, labelled as the Planck length (1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ metres), doubles in size again and again while a step counter climbs. On-screen text asks: How many times must you double this to reach a galaxy? Guess before it ends. At each of 13 stops a step chip appears and copies of the previous object line up across the new one: a proton at step 66, a hydrogen atom at 82, a virus at 92, a red blood cell at 99, an ant at 108, a person (you) at 116, Mount Everest at 129, Earth at 139, the Sun at 146, the solar system at 159, the nearest star at 171, the Milky Way at 185 and the observable universe at 205. Closing text: 205 doublings. From the Planck length to the edge of everything.

first_post.youtube_description:
Start at the Planck length (1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ m), where known physics runs out, and keep doubling. How many doublings until you reach a galaxy? Guess before it ends, then put your number in the comments.

The stops:
66 · a proton
82 · a hydrogen atom
92 · a virus
99 · a red blood cell
108 · an ant
116 · you
129 · Mount Everest
139 · Earth
146 · the Sun
159 · the solar system
171 · the nearest star
??? · the Milky Way (your guess)
205 · the observable universe

Step numbers are rounded to whole doublings. Sizes used: Planck length 1.616 × 10⁻³⁵ m · proton 1.68 fm · hydrogen atom 0.106 nm · virus 100 nm · red blood cell 7.5 µm · ant 4 mm · you 1.7 m · Everest 8,849 m · Earth 12,742 km · Sun 1.39 million km · solar system 60.1 AU (Neptune's orbit) · Proxima Centauri 4.25 light-years · Milky Way 100,000 light-years · observable universe 93 billion light-years.
